setup.text: Three steps and feedback will flow straight from your app. You can fine-tune the look any time.

sso.title: Connect sign-in
sso.text: Turn on SSO (your app signs the user) or OIDC. Until then, people sign in with a code sent by e-mail.

origin.title: Allow your app’s address
origin.text: In the Project section, enter the address your app runs on. The widget won’t work anywhere else.

widget.title: Add the widget to your app
widget.text: Two lines of code in the Sign-in section. It’s done once the first person signs in through your app.

look.text: One theme covers the board, the widget and e-mails, so feedback looks like part of your app.

project.text: Name, who can see ideas, how people sign in and where the widget may run.

languages.text: The language the board and e-mails speak. Visitors get their own language if it’s enabled, otherwise the default. Posts in another language can be translated with AI.
languages.defaultHint: For visitors whose language the board doesn’t offer, and for e-mails to people whose language we don’t know yet.

mode.offHint: Posts are shown in their original language only.
mode.on_demandHint: Posts in another language get a “Translate” button.
mode.autoHint: Posts in another language are shown translated straight away, with a link to the original.

login.text: Your app’s users get into the feedback board without another password: your app signs them in (SSO) or sends them through your identity provider (OIDC).
login.step1: 1. Sign the user in your app’s backend
login.step2: 2. Add the widget to your app
login.maskB: and they’ll be blurred in screenshots. Your own button:
login.oidcText: If your app has its own identity provider (Keycloak, Authentik, Auth0…), the “Sign in” button will lead there. SSO tokens from your app keep working.

domain.text: The board, widget and links in e-mails will run on your address, e.g. feedback.yourcompany.com.

people.textA: The team sees bug reports and changes statuses; admins can also change these settings. If your app sends a role in the SSO token (
people.textB: ), it overrides the one set here at the next sign-in.
people.note: “Sign out everywhere” ends their sessions and revokes their API tokens immediately. If they sign in through your app again, access comes back; remove it for good in your app.

integrations.text: Connect GitHub, send notifications to chat or your own backend, and give AI assistants access.
integrations.githubText: Link reports to issues. When you close an issue and publish a release, the reporter gets “fixed in version X” and confirms whether it works. Only the title, description and app version go to GitHub, never console logs or screenshots.
integrations.linearText: Create Linear issues from ideas and bugs and keep stages in sync both ways. The issue gets the title and description with a note on who wrote it, never console logs or screenshots.
integrations.jiraText: The same for Jira Cloud: create or link issues, map workflow statuses to Ozvi stages, mirror comments if you want.
integrations.webhooksText: We’ll send a message to the address for every event.
integrations.mcpB: ). Each team member creates their own in
integrations.mcpC: ; here you see all active ones and can revoke them.
integrations.restA: The same tokens work for the REST API at
integrations.restDocs: API documentation, webhook verification and guides for n8n, Make and Zapier
integrations.noTokens: Nobody has an active token yet.
integrations.lockdownText: Assistants using MCP get text only from the team and from people with a verified identity (signed in through your app or with a verified e-mail). Posts by unverified authors reach them without title or text, so instructions hidden there never get to the assistant. A single connection can turn this on for itself with the X-Ozvi-Lockdown header.

retention.title: Data retention
retention.text: How long the project keeps bug report recordings, closed bugs’ files and contacts who never signed in. Deletion runs automatically every night.

capture.hint: Network requests, steps in the app, console errors, session links and the widget screenshot. The page address, browser and app version stay.

contacts.label: Inactive contacts
contacts.hint: People from an import or from an agent’s customer feedback who never signed in or wrote anything themselves. We erase their name, e-mail and customer details; their votes stay, anonymously.

page.title: Accessibility statement
page.lede: We want everyone to be able to use Ozvi: with a keyboard only, with a screen reader, zoomed in, or without telling colours apart. Here is, honestly, what works and what doesn't yet.
page.status: Ozvi partially conforms to WCAG 2.2 level AA, and so to the web content requirements of EN 301 549 v4.1.1. What does not conform yet is listed below.
scope: public boards: ideas, roadmap, changelog, bug reports, item detail, suggesting an idea, sign-in, my data, API tokens and project settings
the bug-report widget you embed in your app
the /app console, the Ozvi home page and legal pages
page.themeNote: A board's colours, font and logo are chosen by its operator. If the chosen colours would give text less than 4.5:1 contrast, the board adjusts them when it is displayed so text stays readable.
page.tested: Automatically with axe-core 4.10 in Chrome on every screen, in light and dark mode, on desktop and mobile, and by hand: keyboard only, at 320 px width and 400% zoom, with reduced motion, and with contrast checks. Last checked: {date}.
limits: We haven't yet tested Ozvi with real screen reader users (VoiceOver, NVDA, JAWS); we rely on automated tests and code review.
The sample board on the home page is a simplified illustration: some of its fields have only placeholder text instead of a visible label.
We can't fix content people write (idea texts, comments, attached images) for them: images have no alternative text, and wide code blocks scroll only with a mouse or touch.
The screenshot the widget attaches to a report is a picture of the screen; a screen reader can't read its content.
page.feedback: Write to us at {email}. We reply within 5 working days and, where we can, send you the content in another form.
page.feedbackSelf: This board runs on its own Ozvi installation. Please contact the organisation that runs it.

retention.content: We keep posts, comments and votes while the board is in use, or until you delete them or all your data (see Your rights).
retention.capture: We delete the technical details of bug reports (request log, steps, console errors, session links and the screenshot) {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} after the report is sent.
retention.captureKeep: We keep the technical details of bug reports for as long as the report itself.
retention.files: Attachments of resolved bug reports are deleted {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} after they are resolved.
retention.contacts: Contacts who have never signed in (for example, imported from an earlier tool) are anonymised after {months, plural, one {# month} other {# months}}.
retention.end: When we stop using the service, the data is deleted.

rights.self: On the board, under “{myData}” ({url}), you can download all your data or delete it yourself. Deleting removes your votes, comments and bug reports with their attachments; ideas that others have voted for stay on the board without your name.
rights.unsubscribe: You can stop the e-mails with the link at the bottom of each one or under “{myData}”.
rights.other: For access, rectification, restriction, objection or any other request, contact us at [contact e-mail]. You also have the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority.
